title: An unprecedented weapon? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen quotes Roland Ennos's The Powerful Primate on Edward I's trebuchet Warwolf -- a 60-foot machine delivering ~500 kilojoules, a thousand times a Roman ballista -- and frames it as a medieval step-change in weaponized energy, joking about whether England had a 'pause' movement, an unmistakable analogy to today's calls to halt AI development.

insights.claim: Calls to halt a powerful new technology are not unique to the modern era; Cowen implicitly analogizes today's AI pause movement to the arrival of medieval siege weapons that delivered an unprecedented jump in destructive capability.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Framing pause demands as a recurring historical reflex rather than a novel response argues against pricing in durable regulatory halts to frontier AI capability.

insights.claim: Edward I's trebuchet Warwolf stood over sixty feet high and could throw a three-hundred-pound rock several hundred yards, projecting roughly five hundred kilojoules -- a thousand times the energy of a Roman ballista and five thousand times that of a single person.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Quantifying a pre-industrial capability jump of 1,000x gives a historical base rate for how large a single-generation technology discontinuity can be.
insights.quote: projecting some five hundred kilojoules of energy, a thousand times the power of Roman ballistas and five thousand times as powerful as a single person
insights.locator: Trebuchets reached the peak of their development

insights.claim: The Scots defending Stirling Castle in 1304 sued for peace before Warwolf was ever fired, but Edward I refused to accept their surrender until he had tested the machine, which then destroyed a curtain wall in four days.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A canonical case that possessors of a new superweapon want a public demonstration even when deterrence has already won -- relevant to how states will behave with novel capabilities rather than quietly holding them.
insights.quote: The defenders were so petrified by the prospect of the attack that they sued for peace before Warwolf could be used, but Edward refused to let them surrender until he had tested the machine
insights.locator: Edward used it just once, in 1304

themes.theme: Energy control as the engine of civilization

insights.claim: Roland Ennos's The Powerful Primate argues that humanity's ability to control and concentrate energy is what enabled the building of civilization, with weapons like Warwolf as illustrations of harnessed energy density.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: An energy-throughput lens on civilizational progress supports treating power availability, not software alone, as the binding constraint on the next capability jump.
insights.quote: That is from the new and interesting The Powerful Primate: How Controlling Energy Enabled us to Build Civilization, by Roland Ennos.
